reason: The text is from Nehemiah 2 and repeatedly emphasizes God's 'good hand' (יַד־ אֱלֹהַי הַטּוֹבָה) upon Nehemiah and His support for restoring Jerusalem. The entire narrative frames the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls as a divinely-sanctioned project for the welfare of the Hebrew people. Key evidence: (1) Nehemiah's prayer to 'the God of heaven' for success; (2) explicit references to 'the good hand of my God' being upon him; (3) the people's unified response motivated by trust in God: 'the God of heaven will give us success'; (4) the framing of restoration as deliverance from disgrace and ruin. The narrative structure presents God's providential care and blessing as essential to the people's well-being and recovery.
